text:
maya: FYI seeing a sustained scrub backlog + nvme crc warnings in us-central1-cohort5 starting ~14:10 UTC. GPU attach errors spiked and several batch pods were forced to fall back.

tom: errors? can you paste logs / smartctl?

maya: pasted top lines, lots of repeated CRCs and then scrub job queue pileup. short sample: ```Apr 22 14:11:02 host kernel: nvme0: crc error on namespace 1 sector 2345678
Apr 22 14:11:03 host janitor[2278]: enqueue scrub cohort=cohort5 host=host-234 delay=0s
Apr 22 14:11:03 host janitor[2278]: scheduling scrub failed: rate-limit (429)
Apr 22 14:12:10 host kubelet: attach failed: context deadline exceeded
```

anita: hmm crc errors usually mean drive firmware flapping or weird IO patterns. are the drives on the same firmware cohort?

maya: yes, all nvme P3700-ish on fw 2.14. we shipped a small fw bump two weeks ago but only some nodes got it. host mapping shows a mixed fleet. also noticed network retransmits on the storage control plane at the same timeframe.

raj: mixed-firmware + control-plane retries = good recipe for janitor thrash. scrub tasks are hitting the control-plane scheduler which is rate-limiting; tasks back up and then multiple scrubs hit hosts at once -> IO storm.

tom: can we isolate: 1) cordon the worst 6 hosts in cohort5, 2) pause new scrub scheduling for cohort5, 3) set attach soft-retry to 3m so autoscaler doesn't immediately kick to fallback? thoughts?

maya: agree with 1 & 2 short-term. patching scheduler now to add a 600s cooldown for cohort5. ops-bot: "runbook: scheduler set-backoff --cohort cohort5 --dur 600s requested by maya"

anita: cordon also prevents future batch pods landing on those hosts while we triage firmware. can we requeue scrub jobs onto healthy cohorts instead?

raj: we can stealth-migrate scrub backlog to cohort3 which has spare SSD margin, but that's costly and will increase wear there. recommend migrating only high-priority checks (checksum fixes) and deferring metadata-only scrubs.

tom: prioritization sounds right. also have we considered enabling nvme write-combining at kernel level on affected hosts temporarily? that might reduce tinywrite pressure. risk?

anita: write-combining could mask underlying CRCs and make debugging harder. I'd avoid it unless necessary. prefer reducing concurrency and coalescing scrub windows.

maya: executed: cordon host-231..host-236 at 14:14 UTC, scheduler backoff applied at 14:15 UTC. increased attach soft-retry timeout: `gpu_attach_timeout=180s -> 300s` in autoscaler config and rolled to us-central1 canary.

ops-bot: "action: migrate_scrub_jobs --from cohort5 --to cohort3 --filter high_priority_checks --limit 20 jobs"

raj: monitoring queries: `sum(rate(nvme_io_time_seconds_total[2m])) by (cohort)` and `sum(increase(janitor_jobs_failed_total[5m]))` - watching for drop in failed scheduling and nvme avgqu.

maya: initial impact: attach failure rate dropped from 6% -> 0.8% within 6m, avgqu-sz reduced from ~9 -> ~2 on remaining hosts. we did see a short uptick in wear on cohort3; ops already flagged a maintenance ticket.

tom: estimated cost delta due to fallback and migration ~+$850 for the hour. please log in incident-costs.

anita: follow-ups: 1) audit firmware parity across fleet (schedule mass roll with canary), 2) add scheduler backpressure hysteresis so scrubs don't pile, 3) rethink scrub priority labels (metadata vs checksum) so we can migrate safely.

maya: filing the follow-up tickets now and pinging firmware team. leaving cordons in place for 2 hours and will slowly uncordon as we validate. will open a short postmortem if anything reoccurs. :white_check_mark:
